title: Cap. IX Arg. 12 (Corvinus): absolute reprobation blocks public prayers offered with due faith that the Word will profit all hearers
latin: Isti non recte explicant doctrinam reprobationis, qui talem statuunt reprobationem, quae impediat quo minus publicae preces Deo offerri possint cum debita fide et fiducia quod omnibus verbum Dei audientibus sint profutura. Nam quis animum inducere potest ut pro eorum salute oret, quos Deus aeterna et antecedente voluntate damnare voluit? Apostolus hoc argumento nos acuit ad precandum pro omnibus, quia Deus vult omnes salvos fieri.
pass_a: Those do not rightly explain the doctrine of reprobation, who establish such a reprobation as would hinder that public prayers cannot be offered unto God with due faith and confidence that they will be profitable unto all hearing the word of God. For who can bring it into his mind that he should pray for the salvation of those whom God by an everlasting and antecedent will has willed to damn? The Apostle with this argument sharpens us unto praying for all, because God wills all to be saved.
pass_b: They do not rightly explain reprobation who set such a reprobation as would block public prayers from being offered to God with due faith and confidence that the Word will profit all who hear it. Who can bring himself to pray for the salvation of those God by an eternal antecedent will has willed to damn? The Apostle sharpens us to pray for all with this argument: God wills all to be saved.

lemmas.gloss: Corvinus: reprobation blocks confident public prayer
Apostle's ground for praying for all

title: Cap. IX Arg. 12 Sol: right prayer for others does not require certain faith that our prayers will save them — outcomes are contingent; command to pray for all (even enemies) suffices
latin: Ad preces rite concipiendas pro aliis hominibus non requiritur, ut certitudine fidei nobis persuasum sit, preces nostras illis ad salutem profuturas. Nam fidei nostrae nihil aut falsum aut contingens subesse potest; at plane contingens et incertum est, utrum illi aliquid emolumenti ex precibus nostris sint percepturi. Sufficit quod Deus praeceperit nos omnes homines charitate complecti, et pro aliis, etiam pro inimicis, orare.
pass_a: Unto prayers rightly to be conceived for other men it is not required that it be persuaded unto us by the certainty of faith that our prayers will be profitable unto them unto salvation. For nothing either false or contingent can underlie our faith; but it is plainly contingent and uncertain whether they will perceive any profit from our prayers. It suffices that God has commanded us to embrace all men with charity, and to pray for others, even for enemies.
pass_b: To form prayers rightly for other people, we need not be persuaded by certainty of faith that our prayers will profit them unto salvation. Nothing false or contingent can underlie our faith; yet whether they will gain any profit from our prayers is plainly contingent and uncertain. It is enough that God has commanded us to embrace all men in charity, and to pray for others — even for enemies.

lemmas.gloss: no certainty-of-faith that prayers will save others
command covers prayer even for enemies

title: Cap. IX Arg. 12 Sol: schoolmen — four conditions for certainty of obtaining; praying for another does not always obtain; Major fails that requires certain faith prayers will profit others
latin: Vulgo hoc notum est in Schola Theologorum, qui dicere solent, quatuor conditiones requiri ut oratio alicujus habeat certitudinem impetrandi, quarum una est, ut pro se quis oret. Nam licet sit pia, perseverans, et de pertinentibus ad salutem, tamen si pro alio fiat non semper impetrat oratio. Major itaque propositio, uti videtis, labascit, quae falso supponit preces recte fieri non posse pro aliis, nisi adsit certa fides, quod sint iisdem profuturae. Nec potest nostra de reprobatione doctrina inde refutari, quod ea posita sequatur publicas preces non posse Deo offerri cum fide quod prodessent omnibus verbum Dei audientibus.
pass_a: This is commonly known in the School of Theologians, who are wont to say that four conditions are required that someone's prayer may have certainty of obtaining, of which one is that one pray for himself. For although it be pious, persevering, and of things pertaining unto salvation, yet if it be made for another, prayer does not always obtain. The Major proposition therefore, as you see, totters, which falsely supposes that prayers cannot rightly be made for others unless certain faith be present that they will be profitable unto the same. Nor can our doctrine of reprobation be thence refuted, that it being posited it follows that public prayers cannot be offered unto God with faith that they would profit all hearing the word of God.
pass_b: This is common knowledge in the School of Theologians. They say four conditions are required for a prayer to have certainty of obtaining; one is that one pray for oneself. For though the prayer be pious, persevering, and about things that belong to salvation, yet if it is made for another it does not always obtain. So the Major totters: it falsely assumes prayers cannot rightly be made for others unless certain faith is present that they will profit them. Nor is our doctrine of reprobation refuted by saying that, once posited, public prayers cannot be offered to God with faith that they would profit all who hear the Word.

lemmas.lemma: quatuor conditiones ... ut pro se quis oret
lemmas.gloss: certainty of obtaining needs praying for oneself
Major fails: no need of certain faith prayers profit others

title: Cap. IX Arg. 12 Sol: Minor denied — due confidence is that praying for others pleases God and we obtain as far as he sees fit; stands with our doctrine and with Arminian
latin: Sed pergamus ad Minorem, in qua dicunt reprobationem a nobis positam impedire quo minus preces cum debita fiducia Deo offerantur. Nos hoc negamus, et dicimus ad debitam fiduciam sufficere, quod certi sumus hoc officium orandi pro aliis Deo placere, et nos pro illis impetraturos, quatenus Deo visum fuerit, ac Divinae gloriae fuerit consentaneum. Haec fiducia stare potest aeque cum nostra doctrina, ac cum Arminiana. Nam illi non audent negare decretum reprobationis esse aeternum et irrevocabile, quamvis asserant illud niti aeterna humanae infidelitatis praevisione. Certum itaque est, Judam ab aeterno reprobatum nullis aliorum precibus posse ad salutem perduci, vel posita illa reprobatione quam tuetur Arminius.
pass_a: But let us proceed unto the Minor, in which they say that the reprobation posited by us hinders that prayers cannot be offered unto God with due confidence. We deny this, and say that unto due confidence it suffices that we are certain this duty of praying for others pleases God, and that we shall obtain for them insofar as it shall have seemed good unto God, and shall have been agreeable unto the Divine glory. This confidence can stand equally with our doctrine, and with the Arminian. For they dare not deny that the decree of reprobation is everlasting and irrevocable, although they assert that it rests upon the everlasting foresight of human unbelief. It is certain therefore that Judas reprobated from eternity can by no prayers of others be led unto salvation, even that reprobation being posited which Arminius maintains.
pass_b: But let us take the Minor: they say the reprobation we posit blocks prayers from being offered to God with due confidence. We deny that. Due confidence needs only this: we are certain the duty of praying for others pleases God, and that we shall obtain for them insofar as God sees fit and as agrees with divine glory. That confidence stands as well with our doctrine as with the Arminian. For they dare not deny that the reprobation decree is eternal and irrevocable, though they say it rests on eternal foresight of human unbelief. So it is certain: Judas reprobated from eternity can by no others' prayers be led to salvation — even on the reprobation Arminius maintains.

lemmas.gloss: confidence = duty pleases God; obtain as he wills
even Arminian reprobation: Judas not saved by others' prayers

title: Cap. IX Arg. 12 Sol: their conditional limitations (if they believe, if pertinacity does not hinder) we affirm too — church prayers profit all hearers under those conditions
latin: Sed hic recurrunt ad limitationes illas conditionales; quibus ipsi suum argumentum planissime enervarunt. Nam quando dicunt se non requirere fiduciam absolutam sed conditionalem, nempe ut credamus preces nostras aliis quibuscunque profuturas, si crediderint, si sua pertinacia sibi ipsis non obstent, uno verbo, nisi ipsi sese Divina gratia praestent indignos, hoc et nos totidem verbis affirmare possumus. Non obstante enim decreto reprobationis, certo credimus preces Ecclesiae profuturas omnibus et singulis verbum Dei audientibus, si credant, si sua pertinacia sibi non obsint, et gratia Divina indignos sese reddant.
pass_a: But here they recur unto those conditional limitations; by which they themselves have most plainly enervated their own argument. For when they say that they do not require absolute but conditional confidence, namely that we believe our prayers will be profitable unto any others whatsoever, if they shall have believed, if by their own pertinacity they do not oppose themselves, in one word, unless they themselves render themselves unworthy of Divine grace — this we also can affirm in so many words. For notwithstanding the decree of reprobation, we certainly believe that the prayers of the Church will be profitable unto all and singular hearing the word of God, if they believe, if by their own pertinacity they do not oppose themselves, and render themselves unworthy of Divine grace.
pass_b: But here they fall back on those conditional limitations — by which they themselves most plainly enervate their argument. When they say they require not absolute but conditional confidence — namely that we believe our prayers will profit any others if they believe, if their own pertinacity does not hinder them, in a word unless they make themselves unworthy of divine grace — we can affirm the same in so many words. For notwithstanding the reprobation decree, we certainly believe the Church's prayers will profit all and each who hear God's word, if they believe, if their own pertinacity does not hinder them, and they do not make themselves unworthy of divine grace.

lemmas.gloss: conditional confidence they require — we share
church prayers profit hearers if they believe

title: Cap. IX Arg. 12 Sol: we add what they hide — God wills hearers saved if they believe, yet wills not to soften all so they believe; pray for all, treat none as reprobate
latin: At hoc nos addimus, quod illi obstinato silentio cupiunt occultare, Deum, qui vult omnes Evangelium audientes servare si credant, si sua pertinacia sibi minime obsint, non velle tamen omnium eousque misereri ut emolliantur, et credant, et sua pertinacia sibi non obsint, sed electorum tantum; velle autem permittere ut alii suo vitio indurentur, et in sua voluntaria pertinacia permaneant. Quia vero nobis incognitum est cujus vult misereri, et quem vult suae duritiae relinquere, nostrum est pro omnibus orare, ut convertantur, et neminem singulariter pro reprobato habere.
pass_a: But this we add, which they by obstinate silence desire to hide: that God, who wills to save all hearing the Gospel if they believe, if by their own pertinacity they by no means oppose themselves, yet wills not to have mercy on all unto this point that they be softened, and believe, and by their own pertinacity do not oppose themselves, but on the elect only; but wills to permit that others by their own fault be hardened, and remain in their voluntary pertinacity. But because it is unknown unto us of whom he wills to have mercy, and whom he wills to leave unto his own hardness, it is ours to pray for all, that they be converted, and to hold no one singularly for a reprobate.
pass_b: But we add what they by obstinate silence wish to hide. God wills to save all who hear the Gospel if they believe and their own pertinacity does not hinder them. Yet he does not will to have mercy on all so far that they are softened, believe, and cease to hinder themselves — but on the elect only. He wills to permit that others by their own fault be hardened and remain in voluntary pertinacity. Because it is unknown to us of whom he wills to have mercy, and whom he wills to leave to their own hardness, it is ours to pray for all that they be converted, and to treat no one in particular as reprobate.

lemmas.gloss: wills not to soften all hearers — elect only

lemmas.lemma: pro omnibus orare ... neminem ... pro reprobato
lemmas.gloss: pray for all; name none as reprobate

title: Cap. IX Arg. 12 Sol: who prays for one God precisely wills not to save? — secret of election/reprobation unknown; absolute reprobation is not 'damn Judas whether he believe or not'
latin: Sed adhuc urgent; Quis potest in animum inducere ut pro ejus salute oret, quem Deus praecise nolit servari, cum Apostolus hoc argumento nos acuat ad precandum pro omnibus, quia Deus vult omnes salvos fieri? Respondeo primo, Deus non solet hoc arcanum electionis et reprobationis hominibus patefacere; actiones igitur nostrae ad regulam incognitam nec debent, nec possunt conformari. Secundo, in decreto reprobationis absolutae sive praecisae, ut illi loquuntur, Deus non sic statuit apud se, Ego damnabo Judam, sive non credat sive credat, sed, Ego non ita miserebor Judae, ut emolliatur, ut credat, ut denique de facto convertatur et servetur — sicuti in decreto praedestinationis absolutae Deus non dicit, Ego salvabo Petrum, sive credat sive non, sed Ego ita miserebor Petri, ut credat, ut poeniteat, ut servetur. Si igitur per praecisam et absolutam praedestinationem et reprobationem putant nos intelligere nescio quam praecisionem mediorum a fine, chimaeram suam, non sententiam nostram oppugnant.
pass_a: But they still urge; Who can bring it into his mind that he should pray for the salvation of him whom God precisely wills not to be saved, when the Apostle with this argument sharpens us unto praying for all, because God wills all to be saved? I answer first, God is not wont to lay open unto men this secret of election and reprobation; our actions therefore neither ought nor can be conformed unto an unknown rule. Secondly, in the decree of absolute or precise reprobation, as they speak, God has not thus established with himself, I will damn Judas, whether he believe not or believe, but, I will not so have mercy on Judas that he be softened, that he believe, that finally in fact he be converted and saved — as in the decree of absolute predestination God does not say, I will save Peter, whether he believe or not, but I will so have mercy on Peter that he believe, that he repent, that he be saved. If therefore by precise and absolute predestination and reprobation they think we understand I-know-not-what cutting-off of means from the end, they fight their own chimera, not our sentence.
pass_b: But they still urge: Who can bring himself to pray for the salvation of one whom God precisely wills not to save, when the Apostle sharpens us to pray for all because God wills all to be saved? I answer first: God does not usually lay open to men this secret of election and reprobation; so our actions neither ought nor can be conformed to an unknown rule. Second: in the decree of absolute or precise reprobation, as they speak, God has not settled with himself, I will damn Judas whether he believe or not — but, I will not so have mercy on Judas that he be softened, believe, and in fact be converted and saved. Just so in absolute predestination God does not say, I will save Peter whether he believe or not — but, I will so have mercy on Peter that he believe, repent, and be saved. If by precise absolute predestination and reprobation they think we mean some cutting of means from the end, they fight their own chimera, not our view.

lemmas.lemma: non ... Ego damnabo Judam sive credat
lemmas.gloss: absolute reprobation ≠ damn regardless of faith

title: Cap. IX Arg. 12 Sol: 'God wills all to be saved' does not overturn reprobation — election is 'I will make him saved,' not merely 'I will him to be saved'; conditional will to save stands with absolute reprobation
latin: Porro, quod putant reprobationis decreto a nobis posito adversari illud Apostolicum, Deus vult omnes salvos fieri, multum falluntur opinione sua. Nam (ut minime ingrediar prolixam aliquam explicationem verborum, de quibus in initio hujus disputationis multa disseruimus) illud Apostoli, Deus vult omnes salvos fieri, non negat aut evertit illam quam ponimus multorum reprobationem. Sicuti enim electio minime sita est in hac affirmatione, Volo hunc salvum fieri, sed, Volo hunc salvum facere; ita non-electio sive reprobatio non sita est in hac negatione, Nolo hunc salvum fieri, sed, Nolo hunc salvum facere. Admittamus igitur Arminii expositionem, Deum velle omnes salvos fieri, nimirum, ita ut velit eosdem servare sub hac conditione, Si crediderint et perseveraverint; dico hanc voluntatem conditionalem servandi stare posse cum decreto absoluto reprobandi; quia non denotat actum voluntatis Divinae ad personam aliquam singularem servandam terminatum, sed decretum voluntatis Divinae de universali et perpetuo nexu duarum rerum, fidei scilicet et salutis. Unde recte colligamus, si fides perseverans in quacunque singulari persona reperiretur, esset quoque in Deo voluntas eandem personam servandi; sed non recte inferamus, in decreto efficacem gratiam praeparante, et ad vitam infallibiliter ordinante, neminem fuisse a Deo antecedenter praeteritum. Ut verbo expediamus nos ab hac objectione; Sicut nulla pugna est inter haec duo, Deus praedestinavit Paulum ad vitam aeternam, et, Deus damnaret Paulum si non crederet, si non perseveraret, ita nec inter haec duo, Deus non praedestinavit, vel Deus praeteriit et rejecit Judam, et Deus salvaret Judam si crederet et perseveraret. Nam sub conditione velle servare, nec arguit electionem, nec negat reprobationem.
pass_a: Further, that they think that Apostolic saying, God wills all to be saved, is adverse unto the decree of reprobation posited by us, they are much deceived in their opinion. For (that I may by no means enter upon some prolix explanation of the words, of which at the beginning of this disputation we have discussed many things) that of the Apostle, God wills all to be saved, does not deny or overturn that reprobation of many which we place. For as election is by no means situated in this affirmation, I will this one to be saved, but, I will to make this one saved; so non-election or reprobation is not situated in this negation, I will not this one to be saved, but, I will not to make this one saved. Let us therefore admit Arminius's exposition, that God wills all to be saved, namely, so that he wills to save the same under this condition, If they shall have believed and persevered; I say that this conditional will of saving can stand with the absolute decree of reprobating; because it does not denote an act of the Divine will terminated unto saving some singular person, but a decree of the Divine will concerning the universal and perpetual nexus of two things, namely of faith and of salvation. Whence we may rightly gather, if persevering faith were found in any singular person whatsoever, there would also be in God a will of saving the same person; but we may not rightly infer that in the decree preparing efficacious grace, and infallibly ordaining unto life, no one was antecedently passed over by God. That in a word we may free ourselves from this objection; As there is no fight between these two, God predestined Paul unto everlasting life, and, God would damn Paul if he did not believe, if he did not persevere, so neither between these two, God did not predestine, or God passed over and rejected Judas, and God would save Judas if he believed and persevered. For to will to save under a condition neither proves election, nor denies reprobation.
pass_b: Further: they think the Apostolic saying 'God wills all to be saved' fights the reprobation decree we posit. They are much deceived. Without entering the long word-debate we already treated at this disputation's start — that saying does not deny or overturn the reprobation of many we place. Election does not sit in 'I will this one to be saved,' but in 'I will to make this one saved.' So non-election or reprobation does not sit in 'I will not this one to be saved,' but in 'I will not to make this one saved.' Admit Arminius's exposition: God wills all to be saved — namely, wills to save them under this condition, if they believe and persevere. That conditional will to save can stand with an absolute decree to reprobate. It does not denote a divine-will act terminated on saving some singular person, but a decree of the universal perpetual nexus of two things: faith and salvation. So we may rightly gather: if persevering faith were found in any singular person, God would also will to save that person. We may not rightly infer that in the decree preparing efficacious grace and infallibly ordaining to life, no one was antecedently passed over by God. In a word: as there is no fight between 'God predestined Paul to everlasting life' and 'God would damn Paul if he did not believe and persevere,' so neither between 'God did not predestine — or passed over and rejected — Judas' and 'God would save Judas if he believed and persevered.' To will to save under a condition neither proves election nor denies reprobation.

lemmas.lemma: Volo hunc salvum facere / Nolo hunc salvum facere

lemmas.gloss: conditional will-to-save stands with absolute reprobation
Paul/Judas pair: condition neither proves elect nor denies reprobate
